title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 59 (Rectification of Register of Members)

content.overview: Section 59 allows any person aggrieved, or any member of the company, or the company, to apply to the Tribunal for rectification of the register of members if the name of any person is entered or omitted without sufficient cause, or default is made or unnecessary delay occurs in entering or omitting a name. The Tribunal may order rectification, payment of damages, and consequential directions. The section also covers the register of debenture-holders and other security holders.
content.glance: Tribunal may rectify register of members (or debenture/security holders) where name entered/omitted without sufficient cause or with default/delay; damages and consequential orders available.
content.study: If the name of any person is, without sufficient cause, entered in or omitted from the register of members of a company, or if default is made or unnecessary delay occurs in entering or omitting a name, the person aggrieved, or any member, or the company, may apply to the Tribunal for rectification of the register. The Tribunal may, after hearing, order rectification, payment by the company of any damages sustained, and such incidental or consequential orders as it thinks fit, including as to costs. The provisions apply to the register of debenture-holders or any other security holders. Current-law framing: identify the register error or delay; establish standing; seek rectification and consequential relief from the Tribunal.

sections.heading: Grounds
sections.body: Name entered or omitted without sufficient cause; or default or unnecessary delay in entering or omitting a name.

sections.heading: Who May Apply
sections.body: The person aggrieved, any member of the company, or the company itself.

sections.heading: Tribunal Powers
sections.body: Order rectification; payment of damages; incidental and consequential directions including costs.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Applies also to registers of debenture-holders and other security holders.

examples.title: Wrongful omission
examples.body: A transferee’s name is omitted from the register without sufficient cause. The transferee applies under s. 59 for rectification and damages.

examples.title: Delay in registration
examples.body: Unnecessary delay in entering a transmission on death leads the legal representative to seek rectification under s. 59.

hypotheticals.question: Is s. 59 limited to the register of members?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. It also applies to the register of debenture-holders and any other security holders.

misconceptions.trap: Only the company can apply for rectification.
misconceptions.correction: The person aggrieved, any member, or the company may apply under s. 59.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 59 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify register error or delay. II. Establish standing. III. Seek rectification and damages. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Register facts; ground; standing; damages if claimed; precise relief.
